newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: New consortium seen in Brisbane airport bid.
newsitem.headline: New consortium seen in Brisbane airport bid.

text.p: Queensland government-owned Suncorp Insurance and Finance and Queensland Industry Development Corporation (QIDC) have expressed interest in joining a new consortium bidding for Brisbane international airport, the Courier-Mail newspaper said on Thursday.

The Courier-Mail quoted David Graham, managing director of the Suncorp-owned merchant bank Graham & Company as saying Suncorp was a potential equity investor in Queensland Airport Corporation Ltd, a new consortium with the Cairns Port Authority as operator.

QIDC was to be a debt provider for the project and the consortium was expected to lodge a bid in line with other offers, the newspaper said. Bids for Brisbane airport are estimated to be around A$400 million.
Queensland Airport Corporation (QAC) is jointly held by Bankers Trust Management and Hastings Funds Management's infrastructure investor, Utilities Trust of Australia, the newspaper said.
"There will be opportunity made for Queensland and other institutions to invest but it has been underwritten by BT and Hastings," Graham told the newspaper.
Lead banker to the airport bid would be Toronto Dominion Bank.

The newspaper also quoted Graham as saying the involvement of Cairns Port Authority as an operator of Cairns airport in north Queensland, would provide a major advantage in the competitive bidding process.
Other bidding participants included the British Airports Authority-AMP Society Ltd consortium as well as the Dutch Schipol airport-Comonwealth Bank of Australia group.
